source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 44 MW of IT capacity across three buildings, NVA1 through NVA3, with 420,000 square feet of technical space. That is enough to rank it fifteenth in Virginia by published megawatts, in a state this data counts at 2,563.4 MW across 29 facilities that publish a figure.

The pattern worth noting is the gap between what is mapped and what is measured. Virginia has 376 mapped facilities but only 29 that publish a capacity number. The facilities that publish are the ones large enough to be counted, and most of the physical buildout in the densest data center market in the country is invisible in capacity terms.

For AI specifically, the published figure is a power number, not an accelerator number. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 44 MW is roughly 1,100 racks. At a traditional 8 kW per rack it is about 5,500. The campus is sized to matter at either density, but the accelerator count depends on a density the operator has not published.

The certifications, SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and TIA-942, are permissions to host categories of work, not evidence that any particular tenant is present. The data does not include an address, a postal code, a tenant list, a power procurement method, or a delivery schedule, so it places the campus in the Northern Virginia grid load without saying who runs inside it.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
